tasks.title: The Deerstalker Express
tasks.instructions: Read each paragraph in the time given, then answer rapid-fire questions about it before the clock runs out. Press Enter to submit an answer.

paragraphs.text: The journey began on a September evening in London as a black cab rushed me to Euston station. I had a weekend to myself, and I meant to make the most of it by hitting the famous Highlands of Scotland on a Caledonian Sleeper, a working train also affectionately known as the Deerstalker Express. I saw it as an escape from hectic city life.

paragraphs.text: As the train pulled out of the station just after eleven at night, a friendly steward showed me to my cabin and offered a dram of whisky before bed. I fell asleep almost immediately, lulled by the gentle rocking of the carriage, and only woke when the first grey light of dawn crept through a gap in the curtains somewhere north of the border.

paragraphs.text: By the time I reached the dining car for breakfast, the train was already deep in the Highlands, winding beside lochs so still they looked like sheets of glass. A waiter recommended the porridge with a splash of whisky on top, a local tradition I hadn't expected to see on a train menu.

paragraphs.text: The Deerstalker Express finally pulled into Fort William just before ten in the morning, right on schedule despite the overnight journey. Stepping onto the platform, I felt as though I had travelled not just three hundred miles north, but back in time to a slower, more romantic way of seeing the country.
